title.en: Prime Time: factors, primes and divisibility

text.en:
"Some cicadas sleep underground for 13 or 17 years before emerging—never 12 or 15!" read Leo.
"Wait—why 13 and 17 specifically?!"

A factor of a number divides it with zero remainder, while a multiple is obtained by multiplying it by 1, 2, 3....
A Prime Number greater than 1 has exactly two factors: 1 and itself (such as 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17). A Composite Number has more than two factors; 1 is neither prime nor composite!
Using the Sieve of Eratosthenes, prime factorisation (like 36 = 2×2×3×3), co-prime tests and divisibility shortcuts (2, 3, 5, 9, 10), you can break any big number down cleanly.
Every whole number can be built—or broken apart—using Factors and Multiples.
Factors divide a number completely with zero remainder: factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.
Multiples go upward infinitely by multiplying: multiples of 5 are 5, 10, 15, 20, 25...
Now check which numbers greater than 1 have ONLY two factors—1 and themselves: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13! These are Prime Numbers.
Remember two crucial facts: 2 is the ONLY even prime number, and 1 is NEITHER prime nor composite!

board.text: 2 is only even prime; 1 is neither

text.en: Greek scholar Eratosthenes invented a clever Sieve: cross out multiples of 2, 3, 5, 7 up to 100—what survives are all 25 primes below 100!
Two numbers sharing ONLY 1 as a common factor—even like 8 and 15—are called Co-Prime Numbers.
Want instant divisibility shortcuts without long division? Ends in even digit -> ÷ 2; ends in 0 or 5 -> ÷ 5; ends in 0 -> ÷ 10!
Add digits for 3 and 9! If digit sum divides by 3 (or 9), the whole number divides cleanly by 3 (or 9) too!
Finally, Prime Factorisation factors any number into prime building blocks—like 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5, unique for every number!

problem.en: Check if 4,365 is divisible by 3, 5 and 9 using quick tests, then write its prime factorisation.

why.en: 4,365 ends in 5, so it is divisible by 5.
18 divides by both 3 and 9, so 4,365 is divisible by both 3 and 9!

prompt.en: Are 9 and 16 co-prime even though neither 9 nor 16 is a prime number?

requiredIdeas.en: Yes! Factors of 9 are {1, 3, 9} and of 16 are {1, 2, 4, 8, 16}.
Their only common factor is 1, so they are co-prime.

commonMisconceptions.en: Only two prime numbers can be co-prime.

points.en: Prime: >1 with only 2 factors (1 & self); 1 is neither.
2 is the smallest and only even prime.
Co-prime numbers have only 1 as a common factor.
